source.version: IEEE version of record, 2025 7th International Conference on Computer Science and Technologies in Education (CSTE), pp. 661-665, DOI 10.1109/CSTE64638.2025.11091881 (IEEE Xplore download)
source.title_on_document: Empower or Disempower: The Impact of Generative Artificial Intelligence on College Students' Creativity

supplement.holds: The paper refers to no supplement or online appendix. All statistics are in the text and Table II (p. 664).

paper_design_summary: 113 undergraduates at a university in Gansu Province, China, were randomly assigned to draw an alien in 10 minutes either with the Kimi.AI web interface open (n = 58) or without AI (n = 55), in a psychology laboratory, with the two groups tested separately. Two independent coders rated each drawing for overall creativity (7-point scale), similarity to Earth creatures (two 7-point items), and atypical features (five items). A brick Alternative Uses Test before assignment served as a baseline balance check.

studies.label: Lab experiment: draw an alien with or without Kimi.AI

assignment.what_was_assigned: Use of the generative AI tool Kimi.AI (pre-opened web interface) versus no AI tool while drawing an alien
assignment.quote: Next, the participants were randomly assigned to either the group using GAI tools or the group not using such tools.
assignment.locator: p. 663 (PDF p. 3), Sec. II.B Experimental Procedure; also p. 662, Sec. II.B: "single-factor between-subjects experimental design"

arms.name: GAI (Yes)
arms.description: Drew the alien in a computer-equipped laboratory with the Kimi.AI web interface pre-opened and instructions on how to use it

arms.name: No GAI (No)
arms.description: Completed the drawing task independently without GAI tools

participants.exclusions: None reported. The paper says 113 students were recruited and randomly assigned; Table I (N=58/55) and Table II (Yes N=58, No N=55) sum to 113. The arm counts come from Table I, filled in before the task began.
participants.who: Undergraduate students at a comprehensive university in Gansu Province; mean age 19.71 (SD 0.89); 55 male, 58 female
participants.quote: A total of 113 college students were recruited for the experiment, with an average age of 19.71 years (standard deviation = 0.89), including 55 males and 58 females.
participants.locator: p. 662, Sec. II.A Study Design; p. 663, Table I (N=58/55); p. 664, Table II

ai_tool.how_used: The AI group did the task on a pre-opened Kimi.AI web interface after a brief introduction to its operation. The paper does not describe how participants used it for the drawing or whether they generated images.

task.description: Maddux and Galinsky (2009) structured imagination task: imagine traveling to a planet in another galaxy inhabited by aliens and draw a picture of the aliens

outcomes.name: Overall creativity of the alien drawing ("Total Creativity")
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Two independent coders, unrelated to the experiment, rated each drawing on a 7-point scale (1 = not creative at all, 7 = highly creative); scores of the two coders averaged; ICC = 0.87. The coders' expertise is not stated.

contrasts.reported: Table II: Yes N=(58) M 6.03, SD 0.90; No N=(55) M 4.71, SD 1.34. Text: t (113) = 6.20, p = 0.002, d = 1.16. The text says "The unused group novelty score was higher (M = 6.03, SD = 0.90) than in the unused group (M = 4.71, SD = 1.34)"; Table II assigns 6.03 to the GAI group.
contrasts.locator: p. 664, Sec. III.B Creativity and Table II

outcomes.name: Similarity to Earth creatures ("Similarity to Terrestrial Life")
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Two items (similarity to humans, similarity to other Earth animals), each on a 7-point scale; arm means of about 11 to 13 suggest the two items are summed. Two coders averaged; ICC = 0.63. Higher similarity means a less original drawing, so the sign is reversed relative to creativity: here the GAI group scored higher similarity, which is less original.

contrasts.reported: Table II: Yes N=(58) M 12.87, SD 0.75; No N=(55) M 10.90, SD 1.23. Text: t (113) = 10.33, p <0.001, d = 1.93. The text says "The earth biological similarity in the unused group (M =12.87, SD = 0.75) was higher than in the unused group (M = 10.90, SD = 1.23)"; Table II assigns 12.87 to the GAI group. Direction refers to the similarity score as printed (GAI higher similarity = less original).
contrasts.locator: p. 664, Sec. III.B Creativity and Table II

outcomes.name: Atypical features of the alien ("Atypical Characteristics")
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Five items on sensory organs and body characteristics: absence of organs or body parts, unusual quantities, uncommon shapes, unusual functions, special abilities. Two coders averaged; ICC = 0.91. Higher = more atypical (more original).

contrasts.reported: Table II: Yes N=(58) M 3.68, SD 1.03; No N=(55) M 2.08, SD 0.77. Text: t (113) = 9.27, p = 0.005 and d = 1.76; "It was more atypical (M = 3.68, SD= 1.03) than the unused group (M = 2.08, SD = 0.77)."
contrasts.locator: p. 664, Sec. III.B Creativity and Table II

company_involvement.description: No company involvement stated. Funding: Fundamental Research Funds for the Central Universities (31920250129).

eligibility.reason: Students were randomly assigned to draw with Kimi.AI or without AI (p. 663, Sec. II.B); 113 people analyzed, 58 vs 55 (Tables I and II); drawings rated by two independent coders for creativity, similarity to Earth creatures, and atypical features (p. 663, Sec. II.C). Caveats: the two groups were tested separately (p. 662), so condition may be confounded with session; no preregistration; the reported statistics contain internal inconsistencies (see notes).

one_line_finding: Students who drew an alien with Kimi.AI available scored higher on rated overall creativity (6.03 vs 4.71, t(113) = 6.20, d = 1.16) and atypical features (3.68 vs 2.08, d = 1.76), but also higher on similarity to Earth creatures (12.87 vs 10.90, d = 1.93) (p. 664, Table II).
open_questions: Is the arm assignment of the means correct? The text labels both means as belonging to the "unused group" for creativity and Earth similarity, while Table II assigns the higher values to the GAI (Yes) group.

Higher similarity to Earth creatures in the GAI group means less original drawings, which conflicts with the higher atypicality and creativity scores and with the paper's conclusion; possibly a labeling error.

Reported t statistics and p-values do not match each other (t = 6.20 with p = 0.002; t = 9.27 with p = 0.005), and df = 113 with N = 113 is inconsistent with an independent-samples t-test (df would be 111).
How did participants use a text chatbot (Kimi.AI) in a drawing task? The paper does not say whether they generated images or only asked for ideas.
Groups were tested separately; whether randomization was at the individual level with group-level sessions, or effectively by session, is not fully clear.
notes: Pre-treatment brick AUT baseline (originality t(113) = 4.09, p = 0.06; fluency t(113) = 0.27, p = 0.17; flexibility t(113) = 3.87, p = 0.26; pp. 662-663) is a balance check, not an outcome, and is not listed. Post-task control variables (familiarity, enjoyment, motivation; Table II) are self-reports and not listed. Coders' expertise is not stated, so measure is coded human_raters. Standard errors are not reported; arm means, SDs, Ns, t, p, and d are printed. The candidate record's note "N=113 with no unit stated" is resolved: 113 are people.
